subtitle: On the dust of Samugarh, a prince’s empty seat crowns another king

panels.shot: epic split composition, half the frame with Dara Shukoh on a war elephant before Agra, the other half with Aurangzeb in armor astride a horse before massed ranks
panels.action: Dara Shukoh & Aurangzeb stand opposed in a vast, hazy battlefield tableau, one raised on an armored elephant near the Yamuna plain, the other on horseback leading Deccan-hardened cavalry, banners of the Mughal sun rippling over dust and heat.

dialogue.text: Samugarh, 1658 CE: on a hot plain near Agra, two sons of Shah Jahan raise the same imperial standard, and an empty elephant howdah decides the Mughal throne.

i18n.hi: समूगढ़, 1658 ई.: आगरा के पास तपती मैदानी ज़मीन पर, शाहजहाँ के दो बेटे एक ही शाही झंडा उठाते हैं, और एक खाली हाथी हौदा तख्त तय करता है।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Agra fort skyline over the Yamuna with armies mustering in the distance
panels.action: In the dawn light the marble domes of Agra Fort glimmer above the Yamuna, while far beyond the river dark masses of tents and lines of men and elephants gather under dust, as Dara Shukoh & Aurangzeb’s banners rise in opposite camps.

dialogue.text: The Mughal Empire is at its height, yet the House of Timur is a house divided; Shah Jahan sickens in Agra, and his sons march not as brothers, but as claimants.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल सल्तनत चरम पर है, पर तैमूर का घराना दो फाड़ है; आगरा में शाहजहाँ बीमार है, और उसके बेटे भाई नहीं, दावेदार बनकर चलते हैं।

panels.shot: medium two-shot contrast, Dara on a cushioned seat with books and courtiers, Aurangzeb in austere armor with Deccan officers
panels.action: Dara Shukoh sits in a rich tent, robes loose, a manuscript resting beside him as officers confer, while in a contrasting frame Aurangzeb stands in plain quilted armor among scarred Deccan captains, his gaze narrow and watchful.

dialogue.text: Dara, favored heir, scholar of many paths, trusts rank and affection; Aurangzeb, seasoned in the Deccan wars, trusts discipline, patience and the weight of steel.

i18n.hi: दारा, लाड़ला वारिस, कई राहों का आलिम, रुतबे और मोहब्बत पर भरोसा करता है; औरंगज़ेब, दक्कन का सिखा हुआ सिपहसालार, अनुशासन, सब्र और लोहे पर।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of opposing camps and troop dispositions marked by standards and elephants
panels.action: From high above, lines of Dara’s larger but uneven host stretch along the Yamuna’s left bank, war elephants massed before his tent, while across the plain Aurangzeb and Murad’s tighter, seasoned formations hold firm behind entrenchments.

dialogue.text: On 29 May, near the village of Samugarh, Dara commands the larger army, but his ranks are a patchwork of hastily raised contingents; Aurangzeb’s line is smaller, yet tempered by the hard school of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: 29 मई को, समूगढ़ गाँव के पास, दारा के पास बड़ी फौज है, पर उसकी क़तारें जल्दबाज़ी में जुटाए दस्तो का जोड़-तोड़ हैं; औरंगज़ेब की पंक्ति छोटी है, पर दक्कन की आग में ढली।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Dara mounting a richly caparisoned war elephant, with Agra’s domes faint in the distance
panels.action: Dara Shukoh climbs into an ornate howdah atop a towering elephant draped in embroidered armor, Agra’s faint marble silhouette behind him, as officers point toward the hazy enemy line.

dialogue.text: Custom and symbol rule the morning; Dara chooses the elephant, the high seat from which Mughal princes have guided victory, and from which their armies read courage or despair.

i18n.hi: सुबह रस्म और निशान बोलते हैं; दारा हाथी चुनता है, वह ऊँचा आसन जहाँ से मुग़ल शहज़ादे जंग सँभालते हैं, और जहाँ से फौजों को हिम्मत या हताशा दिखती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Aurangzeb mounting a horse, with cannons and Murad’s line visible beyond
panels.action: Aurangzeb swings into the saddle of a sturdy horse before lines of artillery and matchlockmen, while Murad’s cavalry wait nearby, their armor dull but ordered.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb rides a horse, closer to his files and guns, content to let his cannons and seasoned wings grind Dara’s unsteady host before closing for the decision.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब घोड़े पर है, सफ़ों और तोपों के क़रीब, मंजूर है कि उसकी तोपें और पुराने बाजू दारा की डगमगाती फौज को पीसें, फिर वह फ़ैसला करे।

panels.shot: dynamic wide battle shot as musket smoke and cannon fire obscure the lines
panels.action: The two armies crash; bright flashes of cannon at the front, clouds of white smoke curling over advancing elephants and shouting infantry as Dara Shukoh’s elephant looms high, while Aurangzeb’s guns pound steadily from behind earthworks.

dialogue.text: Drums roll, cannons bark; under the blinding sun the Yamuna plain turns to smoke and shout, and in that confusion men's trust settles on what they can glimpse—banners, elephants, the distant shape of a prince.

i18n.hi: नगाड़े गरजते हैं, तोपें दहाड़ती हैं; चकाचौंध धूप में यमुना का मैदान धुएँ और चीख में बदल जाता है, और उस धुंध में लोगों का भरोसा बस झलक पर टिकता है—झंडे, हाथी, दूर से दिखता शहज़ादा।

panels.shot: close-up of Dara on the elephant under fire, dust and smoke whipping around him
panels.action: Dara Shukoh stands in the howdah, clutching the rail as shot bursts in the dust around the elephant’s feet, anxious officers below gesturing toward a dangerously pressed wing.

dialogue.text: Reports fly in fragments; a wing yields, another presses forward. From the elephant's height Dara sees only fragments of chaos and must decide when he sees least clearly.

i18n.hi: खबरें टुकड़ों में उड़ती हैं; एक बाजू टूटता, दूसरा धक्का देता है। हाथी की ऊँचाई से दारा बस बिखरी अराजकता देखता है, और उसे वहीँ फ़ैसला लेना है जहाँ सबसे कम साफ़ दिखता है।

panels.shot: tight focus on Dara beginning to dismount the elephant with attendants reaching up, battlefield blurred behind
panels.action: Caught mid-motion, Dara Shukoh is shown lowering himself from the howdah with the help of attendants, one hand on the elephant’s harness, the other reaching for the reins of a waiting horse, while dust veils the background.

dialogue.text: Sources diverge; some say Dara seeks to steady a faltering wing, others that shot has made his elephant unmanageable. All agree on the act itself: the prince leaves his elephant.

i18n.hi: इतिहास बंट जाता है; कोई कहे दारा डगमगाते बाजू को थामने चला, कोई कहे गोलेबारी से हाथी बेक़ाबू हुआ। सब एक बात पर सहमत हैं: शहज़ादा हाथी से उतरता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dara riding away at speed on horseback, the elephant with empty howdah looming behind
panels.action: Dara Shukoh urges his horse forward toward a troubled section of the line, the now empty howdah towering behind him on the battlefield, the elephant starting to turn amidst the smoke.

dialogue.text: He rides off, perhaps to rally, perhaps to seek a clearer view, but the battlefield sees only what the dust will show them: an elephant without its master.

i18n.hi: वह सवार होकर निकलता है, शायद हौसला जुटाने, शायद साफ़ नज़र के लिए, पर मैदान बस धूल में जो दिखे वही मानता है: मालिक के बिना एक हाथी।

panels.shot: wide shot focused on the empty elephant moving slowly back from the front, seen from the perspective of Dara’s infantry ranks
panels.action: From the ranks of Dara’s infantry, the armored elephant with its empty, ornate howdah is seen lumbering rearward through the haze, its mahout tugging nervously as men peer up and point.

dialogue.text: In Mughal war, the prince's elephant is a living standard; when it withdraws empty, men read omens. Bernier recalls how, seeing that vacant howdah, Dara’s soldiers murmured, then whispered of defeat.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल जंग में शहज़ादे का हाथी खुद एक ज़िंदा झंडा है; जब वह खाली लौटे, फ़ौज शकुन पढ़ती है। बर्नियर लिखता है, उस सूने हौदे को देखकर दारा के सिपाही पहले बुदबुदाए, फिर हार की फुसफुसाहट फैल गई।

panels.shot: close-up on a line of common soldiers’ faces turning from hope to alarm as they watch the empty howdah
panels.action: A row of Dara’s soldiers stare upward, eyes widening, mouths half open, as the empty howdah passes with slow, ominous grandeur behind them, dust motes hanging in the air.

dialogue.text: No herald cries retreat, no drum beats surrender; yet in the minds of weary men the empty seat shouts louder than any trumpet—'The prince has fled.'

i18n.hi: कोई नगाड़ा पीछे हटने का एलान नहीं करता, कोई ढोल सरेंडर नहीं बजाता; पर थके सिपाहियों के दिमाग़ में वह खाली गद्दी किसी भी बिगुल से ऊँची चिल्लाती है—‘शहज़ादा भाग गया।’

panels.shot: dynamic shot of Dara’s front line wavering, some men surging forward, others glancing back uncertainly
panels.action: The line of Dara’s troops wavers; some archers still loose arrows ahead, while others turn their heads, bodies twisting between the unseen enemy and the receding elephant, confusion etched on their faces.

dialogue.text: Courage rests on belief as much as on strength. When belief cracks, ranks that moments earlier pressed forward begin to hesitate, and hesitation is the first retreat.

i18n.hi: हिम्मत सिर्फ़ ज़ोर पर नहीं, यक़ीन पर टिकी होती है। यक़ीन चटके तो जो क़तारें अभी आगे धकेल रही थीं, ठिठक जाती हैं, और ठिठकना ही पहला पलायन है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Aurangzeb observing through smoke from horseback, with an officer gesturing excitedly toward Dara’s disordered lines
panels.action: From his horse behind the guns, Aurangzeb leans forward, eyes narrowed, as an officer points through the thinning smoke at patches of disorder in Dara’s host.

dialogue.speaker: dara_shukoh_and_aurangzeb
dialogue.text: Press them now; the field itself fights for us.

i18n.hi: अभी धक्का दो; मैदान खुद हमारे लिए लड़ रहा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of Aurangzeb’s and Murad’s cavalry charging into a fragmenting section of Dara’s army
panels.action: Aurangzeb and Murad’s cavalry sweep forward in ordered lines, lances lowered, riding into a section of Dara’s army where files are already bending and breaking apart, a rising dust cloud swallowing their advance.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb’s Deccan-hardened horse seize the moment like water seeking a breach; iron discipline meets growing doubt, and the plain tilts toward one brother.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब की दक्कन-पक्की घुड़सवार पानी की दरार जैसी घड़ी पकड़ लेती है; लोहे का अनुशासन बढ़ते शक से टकराता है, और मैदान एक भाई की तरफ़ झुक जाता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dara, now on horseback with a small escort, looking back at the unraveling battle
panels.action: Dara Shukoh, dust-streaked and tense on horseback with a handful of retainers, twists in the saddle to stare at the collapsing lines behind him, his features caught between disbelief and dawning fear.

dialogue.speaker: dara_shukoh_and_aurangzeb
dialogue.text: How quickly strength turns to smoke.

i18n.hi: ताक़त कितनी जल्दी धुएँ में बदल जाती है।

panels.shot: wide, slightly elevated shot of the battlefield settling, with Dara’s forces streaming away and Aurangzeb’s banners advancing
panels.action: The field lies strewn with abandoned guns and scattered standards as streams of Dara’s men move away in disarray, while Aurangzeb’s banners advance in measured fashion through lingering smoke.

dialogue.text: By afternoon the struggle is decided; Dara’s host dissolves, and the road to Agra lies open. A single rumor, born from an empty howdah, has guided a thousand feet toward flight.

i18n.hi: दोपहर तक जंग का फैसला हो चुका; दारा की फौज बिखर जाती है, और आगरा की राह खुल जाती है। खाली हौदे से जन्मी एक अफ़वाह हज़ार कदमों को भागने की तरफ़ मोड़ देती है।

panels.shot: somber interior shot of Shah Jahan behind the jharokha lattice in Agra Fort, with Aurangzeb’s forces visible far below
panels.action: Within Agra Fort, Shah Jahan stands behind a carved stone lattice, his figure dim against the light, as tiny figures of Aurangzeb’s troops move like ants on the plains below.

dialogue.text: Soon, Aurangzeb will confine his own father in this same marble fortress, and the emperor who once looked down upon all Hindustan will gaze instead at the Taj he built for a lost wife.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही, औरंगज़ेब इसी संगमरमर क़िले में अपने ही बाप को कैद करेगा, और जो बादशाह कभी सारे हिन्दुस्तान को ऊपर से देखता था, वह अब बस उस ताज को निहारेगा जो उसने खोई बेगम के लिए बनाया था।

panels.shot: intimate, shadowed shot of Dara as a fugitive in simple clothes, moving cautiously through a narrow lane
panels.action: Dara Shukoh, now in plain garments, beard untrimmed, walks hurriedly along a shadowed alley with a small escort, glancing over his shoulder as if the empire itself were pursuing him.

dialogue.text: Dara’s path turns from imperial heir to hunted fugitive; after months of flight and failed alliances, he will be seized, paraded in chains, and in 1659, executed with the sanction of his brother’s court.

i18n.hi: दारा की राह वारिस से मुज़रिम बनती है; महीनों की भाग-दौड़ और नाकाम मेल-मिलाप के बाद वह पकड़ा जाएगा, जंजीरों में घुमाया जाएगा, और 1659 में, भाई की अदालत की मुहर से क़त्ल होगा।

panels.shot: close-up on Aurangzeb seated formally on the Mughal throne, expression controlled, courtiers in attendance
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits upon the Mughal throne beneath a canopy, posture rigid, face composed and unreadable, as rows of courtiers bow, some in awe, some in wary calculation.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb becomes Alamgir, 'Seizer of the World.' His reign will be long, pious in his own understanding, often harsh in policy, and remembered in many tongues with fear, admiration, resentment and debate.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब 'आलमगीर' बनता है, यानी 'दुनिया पकड़ने वाला'। उसका राज लंबा होगा, उसकी नज़र में धार्मिक, सियासत में अक्सर सख़्त, और याद रखा जाएगा डर, इज़्ज़त, रंज और बहस के साथ, कई ज़ुबानों में।

panels.shot: symbolic overhead shot of an abandoned war elephant’s empty howdah in the quiet, with distant outlines of Agra and the Yamuna
panels.action: On a now quiet plain, the same ornate howdah rests empty beside a tethered elephant under the fading light, while far away Agra’s domes and the dark line of the Yamuna lie under a soft haze.

dialogue.text: Samugarh reminds us that power is not decided by numbers alone; in the heat of crisis, a symbol—the prince’s seat, a banner’s tilt—can turn rumor into reality, and belief into the fate of empires.

i18n.hi: समूगढ़ याद दिलाता है कि ताक़त सिर्फ़ गिनती से तय नहीं होती; संकट की गर्मी में एक निशान—शहज़ादे की गद्दी, झंडे का झुकना—अफ़वाह को हक़ीक़त, और यक़ीन को सल्तनतों की तक़दीर बना सकता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: On the dust of Samugarh, a prince’s empty seat crowns another king
subtitle_i18n.hi: समूगढ़ की धूल पर, एक राजकुमार की खाली गद्दी से दूसरा राजा बनता है
